content: 1. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of artemether/lumefantrine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution should be exercised, and monitoring is recommended. 2. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 3. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of asenapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Both asenapine (transdermal) and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 6. Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine can significantly reduce rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. If antacids must be used, they should be administered at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 7. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours after administration. 8. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 10. Both atomoxetine and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Calcium acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 13. Calcium carbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 14. Calcium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 15. Calcium citrate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 16. Calcium gluconate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 17. Calcium/vitamin D decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of chlorpromazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 19. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. H2 antagonists should be administered at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 20. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 21. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of citalopram by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 24. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of clomipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Both clozapine and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Conivaptan increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Crizotinib increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Dose reduction may be needed for co-administered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 28. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of cyclobenzaprine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 29. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dasatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of degarelix by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 31. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of desipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 32. Both deutetrabenazine and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation) may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes and/or sudden death. 33. Didanosine affects rilpivirine metabolism via hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are recommended. This interaction applies to didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution. Didanosine should be administered on an empty stomach at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine (which should be taken with a meal). No dose adjustment is required when rilpivirine is co-administered with didanosine. 34. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of disopyramide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 35. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dofetilide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 36. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dolasetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 37. Both donepezil and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Both doxepin and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dronedarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of droperidol by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 41. Both eliglustat and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Erythromycin base increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of erythromycin base by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 44. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 46. Erythromycin lactobionate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 48. Erythromycin stearate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 50. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of escitalopram by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 51. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 52. Famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Famotidine should be administered at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 53. Both fingolimod and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of flecainide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 55. Fluconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. 56. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of fluconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 57. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of fluoxetine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 58. Fosamprenavir increases the effects of rilpivirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 59. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of foscarnet by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 60. Both rilpivirine and fostemsavir increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 61. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 62. Both gepirone and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 63. Both gilteritinib and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 64. Both granisetron and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 65. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of haloperidol by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 66. Both hydroxyzine and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 67. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Famotidine should be administered at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 68. Ibutilide increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 69. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ibutilide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 70. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of iloperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 71. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of indapamide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 72. Indinavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 73. Isoniazid increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 74. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of isradipine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 75. Itraconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
